By using this app, you agree to the terms below.

1. What this is
The app demonstrates downloading. It is not an ongoing online service. It does not offer an account, membership, or paid feature.

2. Your use
You are responsible for making sure a download address is lawful and that you may obtain the content. You are responsible for downloading, storing, and using content from other sites.

3. Where files go
Downloaded files are written into the private folder of this app and stay on this device. Uninstalling the app or clearing its data also removes those files.

4. No guarantee of a download
A download may fail, stop, or finish incomplete because of the network, the site, the system, or the file itself. The app does not guarantee success, speed, completeness, or that the content will be usable.

5. Stopping
You may stop using the app and uninstall it at any time. If these terms change, the text shown in the app is the one that applies.
No account is collected. Data stays on this device.

This app does not offer an account, and it does not upload a profile about you to a developer server.

1. Stored on this device
Theme, language, download tasks, and progress are stored on this device so the app can remember your choices and resume unfinished downloads.

2. Network requests
A link you enter or tap is sent only to the site that link points to, so the download can finish. The app does not create an account, and it does not collect those links on a developer server.

3. Permissions
Internet access is used for downloads. While a download is running, the system may show one notification so the download can continue and you can see progress. The notification stays on this device.

4. Diagnostic logs
Failures and retries are written to logs on this device to help with troubleshooting. Those logs are not uploaded.

5. Other apps and sites
Opening a finished file hands it to another app on this device. How that app handles the file follows its own rules. A site you visit follows its own rules.

Foreground service, or WorkManager if the system refuses

A notification is shown while downloading. If the system refuses a foreground service, WorkManager is used instead. A killed process does not resume on its own; the next launch continues from the last progress.
